messages:
jess: Hey all — first day setup hiccup. I ran `docker compose up` and the db container immediately exits. Logs show `FATAL: could not create lock file "/var/lib/postgresql/data/postmaster.pid": Permission denied` Any quick ideas?

rahul: Welcome Jess! That usually means the mounted data dir on the host is owned by root or has weird permissions (common on mac w/ colima). Are you using a bind mount like `./dev-db:/var/lib/postgresql/data`? If so try switching to a named volume in docker-compose and re-creating the service.

jess: Yeah it's `./pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data`. I tried `sudo chown -R 999:999 ./pgdata` but it still died.

emily: On mac the UID inside the container may not match. We usually use a named volume to avoid host permissions problems: in compose: `volumes: db_data:` and `- db_data:/var/lib/postgresql/data`. If you need persisted host files, `chown` with the container user helps: `docker run --rm -v $(pwd)/pgdata:/pgdata --user root alpine sh -c "chown -R 999:999 /pgdata"`.

rahul: Also check for stale files — if you previously ran as root there can be root-owned files. `rm -rf ./pgdata` if you don't need the contents and then bring up compose again.

jess: Switched to named volume, container stays running now but my app still can't connect from local host testing. I'm running the app on my laptop (not inside a container). I left `DATABASE_HOST=db` in my .env and it's timing out.

max: If your app runs on host, `db` won't resolve — that's only resolvable inside the compose network. Map the port in compose (e.g., `ports: - "5433:5432"`) and set `DATABASE_HOST=127.0.0.1` and `DATABASE_PORT=5433` in your local env. We use 5433 locally to avoid colliding with host Postgres.

emily: If you instead want to run the app in a container, make sure both services are in the same compose file or specify `networks:` so they share the same network. Inside the app container `psql -h db -U postgres -p 5432 -c '\l'` is a good quick test.

jess: Changing to 5433 and `127.0.0.1` fixed connectivity, thanks. One more thing: running our migrations fails complaining about `ERROR: could not open extension control file for "vector"` — looks like pgvector missing. How do folks manage extensions in dev?

rahul: Two options: 1) Use a Postgres image that already includes pgvector (we have `docker/postgres/Dockerfile` in the repo that installs the extension) and set `build: ./docker/postgres` in compose for the db service. 2) If you're ok with a manual step, run `apt-get update && apt-get install -y postgresql-server-dev-all build-essential` and build the extension inside a custom image. Also note that `docker-entrypoint-initdb.d` scripts only run on first init of the volume, so if you already have an initialized DB you'll need to recreate the volume.

emily: We try to avoid rebuilding images locally every time; our onboarding doc has a prebuilt `local-postgres:14-pgvector` image you can `docker pull` (internal registry) — saves a lot of time. Check `infra/README.md`.

infra-bot: Heads-up: do not commit compiled binaries or local /pgdata to the repo. Use .gitignore and named volumes. See https://internal.redwood.dev/dev-setup/local-db for steps.

jess: Pulled the prebuilt image and migrations ran clean. All set! Thanks everyone and hi all :)

max: Welcome! Ping @devex if you want someone to pair on reproducing the setup on your machine. :thumbsup:
